decision.diagnostic_pass: instrumentation is proven loaded by an input-free subprocess and the live run records exact producer retirement method entry/return timestamps or a bounded trace showing which call remains open at callback release.
decision.stop: One fixture, one dispatch, one public cancel attempt maximum; never replay or retry. Abort before cancellation on mismatch. After cancellation, release the hook at bounded hold end or immediately on exception.
decision.strict_action_outcome: R36 tests the unchanged strict gate: one recorded public interface_cancel, at least 1250 ms callback hold measured from cancel response, at least 21 same-call results polls during the hold, independent same-generation Q-up evidence, and bounded cleanup. Any missing condition is FAIL_OR_UNKNOWN. Runtime task_success remains null; no retries/replay.

hypothesis: After independently proving the fixture is actually in Q-down state, a single held injected Q-up callback and public cancellation will show whether recovery clears that exact key while the hook callback is blocked.

instrumentation.mode: R35 adds a finite 10 ms independent same-generation state series process, started before dispatch, to avoid post-event process startup latency. resource_boundary: One user-authorized local Windows PC, one owned fixture/window and hook; one dispatch, at most one public cancellation attempt, 1250 ms post-cancel Q-up callback hold with a 3000 ms absolute callback timeout; no retries/replay, no registry change, no WSLc or Docker. Independent state sampler stops while fixture exists.
retry_policy: Input-free frozen-source, predecessor classification, read-only registry and instrumentation preflight; one fresh fixture/dispatch/cancel attempt. Require same-generation Q-down baseline and projected callback duration including cancel timeout plus hold <=2900 ms before one public cancel. Preserve all failures. Never retry or replay.

scope.environment: Native Win32 supervised caller on the user-authorized local Windows PC; WSLc and Docker are not used.
phase_order: phase 1 one fresh fixture/observation/validation/dispatch/cancel; apply existing strict R36 gate
close phase-1 hook, session and fixture; only if strict gate passes, continue
phase 2 one new fixture/process/window and standard MCP session; observe, validate, dispatch once, retrieve the exact result read-only if pending, verify once with independent server-side oracle
no retry, replay or third phase
scope.question: After one strict bounded cancellation/recovery pass, can a fresh fixture generation in a separate standard MCP session complete one exact task whose independent server-side oracle receipt binds the new call, operation, and generation?
scope.reliability: single paired sequence; no reliability estimate
scope.stop: If phase 1 is not STRICT_RELEASE_PASS, do not start phase 2. Preserve all evidence. Any phase-2 mismatch, timeout, duplicate attempt, stale generation, wrong effect, oracle mismatch, or cleanup uncertainty is FAIL_OR_UNKNOWN; never retry.

trial.effect_order: Stage 1 cancellation/recovery and strict release gate complete before stage 2 starts a separate fixture process, target generation, MCP session, call, operation, and task-oracle receipt.
